newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 9.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 9. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto said agriculture remained an important part of the country's development despite growth in the industrial sector.

Bank Indonesia governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the national economy had started to cool but warned that a relaxed monetary stance could cause it to overheat again. He told an annual bankers dinner that monetary policy this year would continue to focus on strengthening macro-economic stability.

A survey shows that Indonesians have strong sense of religious tolerance despite recent evidence to the contrary. A poll of 1,000 people in three major cities of Medan, Jakarta and Surabaya showed the majority, 64.3 percent, do not pick their neighbours because of their religion.

Chief of the socio-political section of the armed forces Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid said the military would soon arrest people suspected of masterminding recent riots in West Java and West Kalimantan.
At least 88.9 million of shares the mining company PT Alter Abadi are scheduled to be listed on the Jakarta Stock Exchange on Thursday despite allegations that the company produced a fake prospectus.
